meta.location: The land of Nephi, and the wilderness toward Zarahemla

world_behind.title: A decision put to an assembly
world_behind.text: Ammon and Limhi gather everyone so they can have the voice of the people on the question. The record has used that phrase once before, when Limhi explained how his grandfather had been made king. Here it names an actual consultation, and seven chapters later it becomes the founding principle of Nephite government.

world_behind.title: Why the sword is off the table
world_behind.text: Verse 2 gives the arithmetic: the Lamanites are too numerous to fight. Three attempts have already failed and cost the colony many of its men. What follows is a change of method after the method ran out.

world_behind.title: Gideon asks permission
world_behind.text: He opens by reminding the king of his own record: you have hearkened to me many times, if I have been of any service. This is the man who drew a sword on the previous king and later stopped this one from searching his own people. He still waits to be granted permission to speak.

world_behind.title: Tribute paid in kind
world_behind.text: The half owed to the Lamanites was delivered as goods, and wine was part of it. Gideon proposes paying the installment due, adding more as a present, and counting on the guards to drink it. Nothing in the plan requires a weapon or a miracle.

world_behind.title: Directions specific enough to follow
world_behind.text: A back pass through the back wall on the back side of the city, a secret pass on the left of the Lamanite camp, then around the land of Shilom and out. This is one of the few places in the book where the geography is specific enough to follow.

world_behind.title: Where this record ends
world_behind.text: The account of Zeniff's colony opened at Mosiah 9 in a first-person voice and has run through three kings and roughly eighty years. It closes here, mid-flight, with the colony absorbed into another nation. Everything after this in the book is told from Zarahemla, and Limhi's people appear again only as a group being counted.

words.text: To take counsel with, in the sense of deliberating together rather than seeking expert advice. Ammon and the king consult with the people, and the verse says why: so that the matter could go to a vote of sorts. The word puts two rulers on the same side of the table as everyone else.

Yielding no return, and so not worth keeping. Gideon uses it of himself as a conditional (if thou hast not found me to be an unprofitable servant). Benjamin had used the same word of the entire nation at its very best (Mosiah 2:21), and the Savior would later put it in the mouth of servants (Luke 17:10) who had done everything asked of them.

A public order announced aloud, the standard instrument of a king in this record. Treated at Mosiah 1:10. Gideon's plan needs one to move the flocks. The escape could not be kept secret from the people it was for. Only the guards were meant not to know.

Without restraint. The verse says the Lamanites did drink freely of the wine Limhi sent, which is the plan's entire mechanism reported in three words. Nothing is said about deception, and nothing is said in judgment either.

A gift given beyond what is owed. Limhi sends the tribute and then sends more wine on top of it. The extra is the part that makes the plan work, and the record calls it by the ordinary word for a courtesy.

Turned, set on a course. They went round about the land of Shilom and bent their course toward Zarahemla. The verb describes a deliberate change of heading partway through a journey. Going the long way around requires one.

phrases.term: That they might have the voice of the people concerning the matter
phrases.text: A king and a foreign envoy putting a question to an assembly. The clause states the purpose of the gathering before reporting any result. That order makes the consulting itself the point.

phrases.term: Thinking to deliver themselves out of bondage by the sword
phrases.text: The option being closed, and the participle does the work. Fighting free is described as something they had been thinking, not something available. Three defeats stand behind this clause and the verse does not mention them.

phrases.term: I will be thy servant and deliver this people out of bondage
phrases.text: A promise in the first person, made by a subject to his own king. It is the last clause of a speech that spent four sentences establishing the speaker's right to be heard, and it commits him to an outcome. Nothing in it is conditional.

phrases.term: Behold the back pass, through the back wall, on the back side of the city
phrases.text: Three uses of one word in fifteen, which is the opposite of elegant and exactly right for a briefing. Both "back pass" and "back wall" occur once in scripture. The sentence reads like a man pointing.

phrases.term: Pay the last tribute of wine to the Lamanites
phrases.text: The word doing the work is "last." Gideon is describing an ordinary obligation and, in one adjective, announcing that it will never be paid again. The guards receive the delivery as routine, which is why it works.

Five words for the end of two generations away. The verse then lists what else he received: their records, and the plates found by the search party. The reunion and the archive arrive in the same sentence.

phrases.term: They could no longer follow their tracks
phrases.text: The escape succeeding, told from the pursuers' side. The army gives up after two days and is lost in the wilderness, which sounds like an ending and is not. What that lost army finds next puts another people into bondage.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: The only option is stated as the only option
verses.text: The record reports the consultation and its result in the same breath: "they could find no way to deliver themselves out of bondage, except it were to take their women and children, their flocks, and their herds, and their tents, and depart into the wilderness." The reason no other course exists is then given as arithmetic, "for the Lamanites being so numerous, it was impossible for the people of Limhi to contend with them." Escape is presented as a conclusion reached by elimination rather than as a plan someone favoured.

verses.label: v. 6
verses.title: One word, three times, in the same clause
verses.text: The plan opens on a piece of geography stated with unusual repetition: "Behold the back pass, through the back wall, on the back side of the city." The same adjective is used three times in fourteen words, which is not how the record describes anything else. What follows is the operational detail that makes the pass usable, "The Lamanites, or the guards of the Lamanites, by night are drunken."

verses.label: v. 7
verses.title: The tribute becomes the weapon
verses.text: The escape turns on the tax the conquerors imposed: "I will go according to thy command and pay the last tribute of wine to the Lamanites, and they will be drunken." The tribute was set at Mosiah 19:28 as the price of survival, and here the final payment is used to disable the guards collecting it. The volume runs the same trick again at Alma 55:8–14, where a Nephite officer supplies wine to Lamanite guards and takes a city without a fight.

verses.label: v. 11–12
verses.title: What a fleeing nation carries
verses.text: The record lists the load twice, once for the livestock and once for everything else: they departed "with their flocks and their herds, and they went round about the land of Shilom in the wilderness," and "they had taken all their gold, and silver, and their precious things, which they could carry, and also their provisions with them." The clause which they could carry is the limit, and it is the only measure of the flight's scale that the chapter gives.

verses.label: v. 14
verses.title: Two sets of records handed over together
verses.text: The record reports the reception in Zarahemla briefly and counts the objects: "Mosiah received them with joy; and he also received their records, and also the records which had been found by the people of Limhi." The second set is the twenty-four plates the search party brought back at Mosiah 8:9 and Mosiah 21:27, and it becomes the book of Ether. A migration of a whole people is summarised in a verse whose second half is about documents.

verses.label: v. 15–16
verses.title: The pursuers are the ones who get lost
verses.text: The chapter closes on a reversal it does not comment on: "after they had pursued them two days, they could no longer follow their tracks; therefore they were lost in the wilderness." The Lamanite army sent after the refugees ends the chapter without a location, and the record gives it two days and then drops it. The people who fled arrive; the ones chasing them do not.

chapter.title: The deliverance is entirely ordinary
chapter.text: No angel, no darkness sent, no plague on the guards. A back gate, a known drinking habit, an extra shipment of wine, and a night march around a hill. After ten chapters of prophecy and judgment, the record narrates the rescue as competence.

chapter.title: Gideon promises what the rescuer could not deliver
chapter.text: Ammon crossed a wilderness to find these people and could only tell them about a man in Zarahemla who owns interpreters. Gideon says he will deliver them, and does. The offer comes from inside the problem rather than from outside it.

chapter.title: Two men call themselves servants in adjacent chapters, to opposite ends
chapter.text: Ammon declines to baptize, considering himself an unworthy servant. Gideon asks to be heard on the grounds that he has not been an unprofitable one. Benjamin had told the whole nation that they would be unprofitable servants at their very best. The same vocabulary supports a refusal and a volunteering.

chapter.title: The escape works and it costs somebody else
chapter.text: Verse 16 states the failure and its duration, "after they had pursued them two days, they could no longer follow their tracks; therefore they were lost in the wilderness." Mosiah 23:30 then identifies that same army by this event, "the armies of the Lamanites, which had followed after the people of king Limhi, had been lost in the wilderness for many days," and reports that they found the priests of Noah. Mosiah 23:37–39 completes the chain, with Alma's people placed under guards and Amulon set over them. The record makes the link itself rather than leaving it to be inferred.

chapter.title: "Lost in the wilderness" is this unit's refrain
chapter.text: It describes Limhi's search party twice, the pursuing army here, and that army again in the next chapter. Everyone who goes into the wilderness in these chapters gets lost, and two of those parties find something they were not looking for.

chapter.title: The voice of the people, on its way to becoming law
chapter.text: It enters the record as a practical measure taken by a king with no good options and a foreign envoy with no authority. Seven chapters later it is the constitutional principle a nation is told to do all its business by.

chapter.title: The records travel with the refugees
chapter.text: Verse 14 puts the people, their records, and the twenty-four plates in one sentence. The Jaredite record reaches Zarahemla as luggage in a night escape, and the chapter spends no more words on it than on the flocks.

chapter.title: Role in the unit
chapter.text: Mosiah 9 and 10 are Zeniff's record, 11 through 17 Noah and Abinadi, 18 Alma leaving, 19 through 22 Limhi's bondage and escape. This closes the first thread. Chapters 23 and 24 go back to pick up Alma's, and 25 brings every surviving group together in one place.

applications.title: Ask before you advise
applications.text: Gideon had standing, a record of being right, and an urgent plan, and he still asked for permission to speak. Having good counsel does not by itself give you the floor.

applications.title: Use what the situation already contains
applications.text: A gate that exists, a habit that exists, an obligation already owed. Before looking for new resources, inventory what is already in play and whether it can be pointed a different direction.

applications.title: Send more than is required
applications.text: The tribute alone would not have been enough; the extra was the plan. Generosity beyond the minimum sometimes accomplishes what the minimum cannot.

applications.title: Notice when the method is the problem
applications.text: Three defeats, then a different approach entirely. If the same instrument keeps failing, the question is not how to wield it better.

applications.title: Put it to the people affected
applications.text: Two leaders with the authority to decide called an assembly instead. When a choice binds everyone, the decision itself is improved by being taken together.

applications.title: Take the records with you
applications.text: They carried gold and provisions and also the writing. In an emergency evacuation of your own, know which of your things are irreplaceable rather than merely valuable.

applications.title: Your success can be someone else's cost
applications.text: The escape sent an army wandering into the path of another people. It is worth asking who is downstream of a plan that works.

questions.text: What decision am I making alone that belongs to more people than me?
What have I tried three times that is not going to work the fourth?
Where could I say "I will do this" instead of describing the problem again?
What exit already exists in a situation I think is closed?
When have I sent only what was owed?
What would I want received with joy, besides myself?
